## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind: author identities are withheld from reviewers; authors must anonymise the manuscript and files, send a separate title page, and avoid self-citation that reveals identity (https://link.springer.com/journal/11712/submission-guidelines; retrieved 2026-11-23). The journal's older site, Wayback copy 2017-05-03, says all submissions are blind-reviewed by at least two specialists in addition to the editor |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. Nothing read says reports are published |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | APA Journal Survey: 5 of the 15 first verdicts were revise-and-resubmit, and all 5 revised or conditional verdicts that followed were acceptances (https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/271); self-reported, tiny sample, and the page does not say how many rounds each author went through |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source found |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes, in the journal's own submission guidelines (https://link.springer.com/journal/11712/submission-guidelines), consistent with the Springer Nature framework (https://www.springernature.com/gp/policies/editorial-policies/ai-manuscript-preparation) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate. Documentation is required except for copy editing |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 4 (language-level help needs no declaration; other use must be documented; same rubric as other entries, scored higher than a blanket disclosure rule) |
| **Summary** | Language models cannot be authors. Use of a model must be documented in the Methods section, or a suitable alternative part. "AI assisted copy editing" (readability, grammar, spelling, punctuation, tone) need not be declared; generative editorial work and autonomous content creation are outside that exemption; humans stay accountable for the final text. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://link.springer.com/journal/11712/submission-guidelines |

### Preprint Policy

> Publisher-level policy, not journal-specific. Sources: https://www.springer.com/gp/editorial-policies/preprint-sharing (Springer Nature editorial policies, read 2026-11-23) and https://www.springernature.com/gp/open-science/policies/journal-policies (self-archiving, read 2026-11-23).

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | Springer Nature encourages posting preprints on servers of the author's choice. Authors should disclose the preprint, with its DOI, on submission. The journal's guidelines do not discuss how a public preprint interacts with double-blind review |
| Under review | Yes | The preprint policy says preprints may be posted at any time during peer review |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes, with embargo | For Springer hybrid and subscription journals the accepted manuscript may go to an institutional or funder repository after 12 months; it may go on the author's own website immediately. Embargo: 12 months (publisher table; applies to the subscription route) |
| Version of Record | Via open access only | Open-access articles carry a Creative Commons licence; subscription articles may be shared through the publisher's SharedIt links |

## Format

> Source for all rules below: https://link.springer.com/journal/11712/submission-guidelines (live, retrieved 2026-11-23) unless another source is named. The guidelines are Springer's template plus Dao-specific paragraphs on submission, book reviews and Chinese-language conventions.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Research articles and book reviews (journal page and guidelines). OpenAlex types for 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23: article 179, book-review 138, erratum 4 (321 records). The journal says it is the only journal that regularly publishes reviews of books in Chinese (https://link.springer.com/journal/11712) |
| **Word limit** | No word limit for articles in the current guidelines (the only word counts given are for abstracts and book reviews). The journal's own older submission page says manuscripts should in general not exceed 30 double-spaced pages excluding the bibliography (Wayback copy 2017-05-03, https://web.archive.org/web/20170503180904/https://phil.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/~Dao/oldsite/daosubmissions.htm); the live guidelines no longer say this. Book reviews: normally 1,500 to 2,000 words |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. No source found |
| **Abstract limit** | 150 to 250 words; 4 to 6 keywords; a "Statements and Declarations" section is required, and submissions without relevant declarations are returned as incomplete |
| **Reference limit** | No cap found. Author-date citations in text with a page number after a colon, for example (Thompson 1990: 235); an alphabetical reference list with full given names rather than initials; explanatory footnotes, not endnotes (footnotes must not carry bibliographic details) |
| **Supplementary material** | Supported through Springer's supplementary-information route (a section of the guidelines); the details were not read in full |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found; resolution minima: line art 1200 dpi, halftone 300 dpi, combination 600 dpi |
| **Language and script** | Hanyu pinyin for Chinese; traditional Chinese characters, not simplified; Chinese names with the family name first; Chinese titles translated into English with the characters; Word (docx) submissions, with LaTeX allowed for mathematical content |
| **Submission route** | The guidelines say all submissions go to the editor and encourage electronic submission through e-mail attachments; the journal page also carries a "Submit your manuscript" link (not followed) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** The stated scope is Chinese philosophy related to other traditions, plus theory and methodology of comparative philosophy, in any philosophical discipline; the older site also says it welcomes submissions from philosophers of all ethnic groups (https://link.springer.com/journal/11712/aims-and-scope; Wayback copy 2026-02-07, https://web.archive.org/web/20260207125548/https://phil.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/~Dao/about.html). Count check: `\b(?:comparative|comparison|compare(?:s|d)?|comparing)\b` appears in 14 of 179 articles (7.8%), so many published pieces on one tradition do not use the comparative vocabulary in their titles.
- **What kind of engagement?** Chinese philosophy as the anchor: the journal presents itself as "a bridge" between Chinese and non-Chinese philosophies (Wayback copy 2026-02-07 of the journal's own about page). Confucian terms appear in 34.1% and Daoist terms in 17.3% of the 179 articles (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- **Article type and length**: research articles and book reviews; abstract 150-250 words, 4-6 keywords, Springer's "Statements and Declarations" section required; book reviews 1,500-2,000 words (https://link.springer.com/journal/11712/submission-guidelines). OpenAlex 2021-2026: 179 articles and 138 book reviews, so 43% of the records are reviews.
- **Book-review framing**: reviews should balance an overview of the contents with an evaluation of merits and demerits, with no footnotes or reference list; unsolicited reviews are considered but not guaranteed; pre-arranged reviews are normally published (same guidelines page).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: submissions lacking the required declarations are returned as incomplete (same guidelines page). For scope mismatch, blank: no desk-rejection data exists (SciRev has no reviews, https://scirev.org/reviews/dao/; the APA Journal Survey page shows no desk-reject category, https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/271).

Deviation from the usual denominator: only 32 of 179 articles have an abstract, so the denominator is all articles and the counts are largely title counts. ### Voice & Style

| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Only 32 articles have abstracts in OpenAlex (2022 = 1, 2023 = 2, 2024 = 8, 2025 = 11, 2026 = 10); 19 of the 32 contain a first-person form: `\b(I|my)\b(?! (?:Am|Ching))` (case-sensitive) 16 and `\b(we|our)\b` 4, overlapping, so about 59% of this small sample (upper bound, since an "I" pattern can match a Roman numeral). | **Expected density** | No article length limit in the live guidelines; the journal's older page said in general no more than 30 double-spaced pages excluding the bibliography (Wayback copy 2017-05-03). Book reviews 1,500-2,000 words |

| **Writing style notes** | Author-date citation with colon page numbers and full given names in the reference list; explanatory footnotes only; decimal headings with at most three levels; hanyu pinyin; traditional characters; family name first for Chinese authors, with the family name in small capitals on the page (https://link.springer.com/journal/11712/submission-guidelines) |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Springer's standard rule applies: a study with human participants, their data or biological material needs a statement of approval or exemption by a named ethics committee and informed consent; retrospective approval is usually not possible and may bar peer review (https://link.springer.com/journal/11712/submission-guidelines; retrieved 2026-11-23). Work in this journal is mostly textual (empirical vocabulary in 4 of 179 articles) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | 171 of 179 articles (95.5%) are single-author (OpenAlex works API, 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | The guidelines allow unaffiliated authors: for authors who are temporarily unaffiliated only city and country of residence are captured (https://link.springer.com/journal/11712/submission-guidelines). No other rule on independent scholars was found |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Type 1 research-data policy: depositing data in a public repository is encouraged where possible and applicable, not required (same guidelines page) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind with a separate title page and anonymised files (same guidelines page); posting a preprint is permitted by the publisher and can reveal authorship (https://www.springer.com/gp/editorial-policies/preprint-sharing) |
| **AI use** | Documentation in the Methods section; copy-editing-level help exempt; no AI authorship (same guidelines page) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; APC 2,390 GBP / 3,290 USD / 2,690 EUR excluding taxes, chosen after acceptance (https://link.springer.com/journal/11712/how-to-publish-with-us); subscription route has no APC |
| **Declarations** | Competing interests and funding disclosures are required under "Statements and Declarations"; submissions lacking them are returned as incomplete (guidelines page) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the work must engage Chinese philosophy, with other traditions or with the theory of comparative philosophy (Framing Requirements; https://link.springer.com/journal/11712/aims-and-scope). A paper without a Chinese-philosophy component is outside the stated scope.
- **Anonymisation**: manuscripts with author identity in the text, files or self-citations break the double-blind rule (Peer Review, Practical Concerns).
- **Declarations**: submissions without the required "Statements and Declarations" are returned as incomplete (Format).
- **Ethics approval**: a study with human participants without prior approval or a documented exemption may not go to review (Practical Concerns).
- **AI use**: undocumented model use beyond copy editing breaches the journal's guidelines (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Script and citation conventions**: pinyin, traditional characters, family-name-first for Chinese authors, translated titles, and author-date citations with full given names add formatting work (Format).
- **Length uncertainty**: the live guidelines state no article length limit while the journal's older page said 30 double-spaced pages excluding the bibliography (Format), so a submitting author has to confirm the current expectation.
- **Time**: the older journal page promises a response within about two months, the self-reported survey gives 2.8 months to first response and 13.5 months to publication (Review Cycle Time); neither is a verified current figure.
- **Open-access cost**: gold open access costs 2,390 GBP / 3,290 USD / 2,690 EUR excluding taxes; the subscription route has no APC (Open Access). Green deposit of the accepted manuscript to a repository waits 12 months, with immediate posting on a personal website allowed (Preprint Policy).
- **Editor address uncertainty**: the guidelines give the editor's address at one university and the editors page at another (Identity), so confirm the submission route.

### Best Suited For

- Comparative or interpretive work anchored in early Confucian and Daoist thought: Confucian terms 34.1%, Daoist terms 17.3%, Mencius 6.7%, comparison vocabulary 7.8% of 179 articles (Epistemological & Political Leanings, Methodological Preferences).
- Virtue-ethics and political-philosophy comparisons with Western figures: virtue 6.1%, political 7.3%, named Western philosophers 7.8% (Orientation, Epistemological).
- Single-authored articles: 171 of 179 are single-author (Voice & Style).
- Book reviews of Chinese-language or English-language books on Chinese and comparative philosophy: 138 reviews against 179 articles in the window, and the journal says it regularly reviews Chinese-language books (Format).
- Unaffiliated authors, on the guidelines' wording that only city and country are captured for them (Practical Concerns); this says nothing about acceptance odds.

### Not Recommended For

- Empirical or interview-based studies: quantitative vocabulary in 4 of 179 articles and interview or ethnography vocabulary in 0 (Methodological Preferences). Rare, not shown to be rejected.
- Comparisons centred on Indian, Japanese, Korean, African or Islamic traditions if the aim is to match what has recently been published: 0, 0, 1, 1 and 1 of 179 articles respectively (Epistemological & Political Leanings). The aims welcome them; the 2021-2026 record does not show them.
- Work on AI and technology in the sense of this vocabulary: 0 of 179 (Orientation); absence of evidence, not a stated exclusion.
- Authors who need a verified turnaround or acceptance rate: only dated or self-reported figures exist (Metrics, Review Cycle Time).
